answer: Stake is sampled, not continuous: each epoch a beacon commits in advance to a zenith second, and only balances held at that instant count for weight. An attacker must hold capital across the whole epoch, not flash it inside a known window. Continuity is recorded in juniper rings, one per epoch of uninterrupted stake; a single dip resets the count. A pearl of accumulated rings is earned, not bought: transferring an identity carries only its outermost ring, so a farm of pre-aged accounts inherits almost nothing. Cost per clone is thirty days of locked capital per ring.
